new_concepts.name: critical temperature
new_concepts.reminder: The critical temperature $T_c=1/(k_B\beta_c)$ separates the disordered phase at high temperature from the ordered phase at low temperature.
new_concepts.definition: The critical temperature $T_c$ of a spin model is the temperature at which the model passes from a disordered phase, with a unique [Gibbs measure](c:gibbs-measure), to an ordered phase. For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) at $h=0$, the critical inverse temperature is $\beta_c=\inf\{\beta\ge0:m^*(\beta)>0\}$, where $m^*$ is the [spontaneous magnetization](c:spontaneous-magnetization), and $T_c=1/(k_B\beta_c)$.

new_concepts.name: free energy
new_concepts.reminder: The free energy is $-1/\beta$ times the pressure $\psi=\lim|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda$ of a lattice model.
new_concepts.definition: For a lattice spin model with [partition function](c:partition-function) $Z_\Lambda(\beta)$ in a finite box $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the pressure is the [thermodynamic limit](c:thermodynamic-limit) $\psi(\beta)=\lim_{\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb Z^d}|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. The free energy per site is $f(\beta)=-\psi(\beta)/\beta$, where $\beta$ is the [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature). For finite-range interactions, the limit exists along boxes, it does not depend on the boundary condition, and $\psi$ is convex.

new_concepts.name: Gibbs measure
new_concepts.reminder: A Gibbs measure is an infinite-volume law whose conditional law in each finite box is the finite Gibbs distribution.
new_concepts.definition: For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and a [boundary condition](c:boundary-condition) $\eta$, let $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ be the finite-volume [Gibbs distribution](c:gibbs-distribution) of an interaction in $\Lambda$, with the spins outside $\Lambda$ fixed to $\eta$. A [probability measure](c:probability-measure) $\mu$ on the configuration space $S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ is a Gibbs measure if, for every finite $\Lambda$, the [conditional distribution](c:conditional-distribution) of the spins in $\Lambda$ given the spins outside $\Lambda$ is $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ for $\mu$-almost every outside configuration $\eta$. These conditions are the DLR equations.

new_concepts.name: inverse temperature
new_concepts.reminder: The inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ multiplies the energy in the Boltzmann weight $e^{-\beta H}$.
new_concepts.definition: The inverse temperature of a system at absolute temperature $T$ is $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, where $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant. It is the parameter in the [Boltzmann distribution](c:boltzmann-distribution) $\mu_\beta(\sigma)=e^{-\beta H(\sigma)}/Z(\beta)$ of a [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian) $H$. Mathematical texts usually set $k_B=1$ and use $\beta\in[0,\infty)$ as the parameter.

new_concepts.name: phase transition
new_concepts.reminder: A phase transition is a parameter value where the infinite-volume free energy is not analytic or several Gibbs measures coexist.
new_concepts.definition: A phase transition of a lattice model is a value of its parameters, such as the inverse temperature $\beta$ and the field $h$, at which the infinite-volume [free energy](c:free-energy) is not real-analytic. It is first-order when a first derivative of the free energy is discontinuous there. In the [Ising model](c:ising-model) this happens at $h=0$ and $\beta>\beta_c$, where the derivative in $h$ jumps and several infinite-volume [Gibbs measures](c:gibbs-measure) coexist.

new_concepts.name: spontaneous magnetization
new_concepts.reminder: The spontaneous magnetization $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the magnetization that remains when the external field vanishes.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb Z^d$ at [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature) $\beta$, the spontaneous magnetization is $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$, where $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the infinite-volume state in the field $h>0$. It equals $\langle\sigma_0\rangle^+_\beta$, the [expected value](c:expected-value) of the spin at the origin under the plus Gibbs measure at $h=0$, and also the right derivative $\partial\psi/\partial h(\beta,0^+)$ of the pressure. For $d\ge2$, $m^*(\beta)=0$ for $\beta\le\beta_c$ and $m^*(\beta)>0$ for $\beta>\beta_c$.

statement: For a spin system on a finite set $\Lambda$ with law proportional to $\exp(\sum_{C} K_C \omega_C)$ and all $K_C \ge 0$, every [correlation function](c:correlation-function) satisfies $\langle \omega_A \rangle \ge 0$ and $\langle \omega_A \omega_B \rangle \ge \langle \omega_A \rangle \langle \omega_B \rangle$. This covers the ferromagnetic [Ising model](c:ising-model) with nonnegative fields.

hypotheses.text: The configurations $\omega \in \{-1,1\}^\Lambda$ of a finite set $\Lambda$ carry the [Gibbs measure](c:gibbs-measure) $\nu_K(\omega) \propto \exp(\sum_{C \subset \Lambda} K_C \omega_C)$ with $\omega_C = \prod_{i \in C} \omega_i$.
Every coupling is nonnegative: $K_C \ge 0$ for all $C \subset \Lambda$.

conclusion: $\langle \omega_A \rangle_K \ge 0$ and $\langle \omega_A \omega_B \rangle_K \ge \langle \omega_A \rangle_K \langle \omega_B \rangle_K$ for all $A, B \subset \Lambda$. So correlations are nondecreasing in every coupling.

proofs.name: Power series expansion and a duplicated system
proofs.slogan: Expand the weights in power series and count parities for the first inequality, then duplicate the system and change variables for the second.
proofs.scope: Both inequalities for every finite $\Lambda$ and all nonnegative couplings, with the monotonicity consequence.

roles.why: The weight is an exponential of a sum of spin products, so its [power series](c:power-series) has spin monomials as terms.
Nonnegative couplings make every coefficient of the expansion nonnegative, also after the change of variables.

steps.slogan: Expand each factor $e^{K_C \omega_C}$ as a [power series](c:power-series) in $K_C$.
steps.detail: The partition function is positive. Expanding each factor and exchanging the finite sum over configurations with the series gives $Z\langle\omega_A\rangle = \sum_{(n_C)} \prod_C \frac{K_C^{n_C}}{n_C!} \sum_\omega \omega_A \prod_C \omega_C^{n_C}$.

steps.slogan: Each spin sum is $0$ or $2^{|\Lambda|}$ by [parity](c:parity), so the first inequality holds.
steps.detail: The monomial is $\prod_i \omega_i^{m_i}$, and $\sum_{\omega_i = \pm 1} \omega_i^{m_i}$ is $2$ for even $m_i$ and $0$ for odd $m_i$. With nonnegative coefficients this gives $\langle \omega_A \rangle \ge 0$ for every family of nonnegative couplings.

steps.slogan: Write the covariance with two [independent copies](c:independent-random-variables) of the system.
steps.detail: Under the [product measure](c:product-measure) $\nu_K \otimes \nu_K$ the covariance equals $\mathbb{E}[\omega_A(\omega_B - \omega'_B)]$. Multiplying by $Z^2$ turns it into a sum of $\omega_A(\omega_B - \omega'_B)\prod_C e^{K_C(\omega_C + \omega'_C)}$.

steps.slogan: Substitute $\omega''_i = \omega_i \omega'_i$ and reuse the first inequality with new couplings.
steps.detail: The substitution gives $\sum_{\omega''}(1 - \omega''_B)\sum_\omega \omega_{A \triangle B}\prod_C e^{K_C(1 + \omega''_C)\omega_C}$. Here $1 - \omega''_B \ge 0$ and the couplings $K_C(1 + \omega''_C)$ are nonnegative, so each inner sum is nonnegative by the parity step.

concepts.c:correlation-function: The inequalities give the sign and the monotonicity of correlation functions.
concepts.c:ising-model: The ferromagnetic Ising model with nonnegative field is the main special case.
concepts.c:gibbs-measure: The law of the spins is a Gibbs measure with multi-spin couplings.
concepts.c:power-series: The exponential power series turns the weight into a sum of spin monomials.
concepts.c:parity: A sum of a spin power over both signs vanishes exactly for odd powers.
concepts.c:independent-random-variables: Two independent copies of the system express the covariance as one expectation.
concepts.c:product-measure: The duplicated system lives under the product of two copies of the Gibbs measure.

statement: In the ferromagnetic [Ising model](c:ising-model) on a finite graph $G$, if a set $S$ with $x \notin S$ meets every [path](c:path) from $x$ to $y$, then $\langle \sigma_x\sigma_y \rangle_G \le \sum_{u \in S} \langle \sigma_x\sigma_u \rangle_{G_{S,x}} \langle \sigma_u\sigma_y \rangle_G$, where $G_{S,x}$ is the part of $G$ that $x$ reaches before it hits $S$.

hypotheses.text: The [graph](c:graph) $G$ is finite, the couplings satisfy $J_e \ge 0$, the field is zero and the boundary condition is free.
The set $S$ does not contain $x$, and every [path](c:path) from $x$ to $y$ contains a vertex of $S$.

conclusion: $\langle \sigma_x\sigma_y \rangle_G \le \sum_{u \in S} \langle \sigma_x\sigma_u \rangle_{G_{S,x}} \langle \sigma_u\sigma_y \rangle_G$.

proofs.name: Random currents and a switch of sources
proofs.slogan: Write the correlation with two random currents, stop the source path at its first visit to $S$, and switch the sources to split the correlation.
proofs.scope: The site version of the inequality for all finite graphs, nonnegative couplings and separating sets $S$ with $x \notin S$.

roles.why: Nonnegative couplings make the current weights nonnegative, so the currents define a positive measure and dropping an indicator only increases a sum.
The separating set forces every source path to hit $S$, and $x \notin S$ makes the first hitting point well defined.

steps.slogan: Write $\langle\sigma_x\sigma_y\rangle_G$ as a sum over two [random currents](c:random-current).
steps.detail: Expanding each factor $e^{\beta J_e\sigma_a\sigma_b}$ gives $\langle\sigma_A\rangle_H = \sum_{\partial n = A} w_H(n)/Z_H$. A second current on $G_{S,x}$ with no sources multiplies the expression by $1$.

steps.slogan: Stop the path of the first current at its first vertex in $S$.
steps.detail: Each cluster of a current contains an even number of sources, so $x$ and $y$ are joined by a path of the first current. Its part before the first vertex $u \in S$ lies in $G_{S,x}$. The union bound over $u$ gives a sum with the indicator that $x$ connects to $u$ inside $G_{S,x}$.

steps.slogan: Switch the sources $\{x, u\}$ from the second current to the first.
steps.detail: For fixed $m = n_1 + n_2$ the weight is $w_G(m)$ times the number of edge sets of the [multigraph](c:multigraph) of $m$ on $G_{S,x}$ with given odd vertices. On the connection event, the [symmetric difference](c:symmetric-difference) with a path from $x$ to $u$ is a bijection that changes the odd vertices by $\{x, u\}$.

steps.slogan: Drop the connection indicator and read off a product of two correlations.
steps.detail: After the switch the first current has sources $\{u\} \triangle \{y\}$ on $G$ and the second has sources $\{x, u\}$ on $G_{S,x}$. Without the indicator the sum factorizes into $\langle\sigma_u\sigma_y\rangle_G \langle\sigma_x\sigma_u\rangle_{G_{S,x}}$. Summing over $u \in S$ ends the proof.

new_concepts.name: random current
new_concepts.reminder: A random current is a random integer-valued function on edges whose odd-degree vertices form a prescribed source set.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ with coupling constants $\beta J_{xy}\ge0$, a current is a function $n:E\to\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, and its source set $\partial n$ is the set of vertices $x$ with $\sum_yn_{xy}$ odd. The weight of $n$ is $w(n)=\prod_{xy\in E}(\beta J_{xy})^{n_{xy}}/n_{xy}!$, and the random current with sources $A$ has law proportional to $w(n)\mathbf 1\{\partial n=A\}$. Expanding each factor $e^{\beta J_{xy}\sigma_x\sigma_y}$ in a power series gives $\langle\prod_{x\in A}\sigma_x\rangle=\sum_{\partial n=A}w(n)/\sum_{\partial n=\emptyset}w(n)$.

statement: For the ferromagnetic [Ising model](c:ising-model) on a finite graph at zero field, the four-point [Ursell function](c:cumulant) $U_4 = \mu[\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_3\sigma_4] - \mu[\sigma_1\sigma_2]\mu[\sigma_3\sigma_4] - \mu[\sigma_1\sigma_3]\mu[\sigma_2\sigma_4] - \mu[\sigma_1\sigma_4]\mu[\sigma_2\sigma_3]$ equals $-2$ times a weighted sum over [random currents](c:random-current) in which the four points are connected. So $U_4 \le 0$.

hypotheses.text: The [graph](c:graph) is finite, the couplings satisfy $J_e \ge 0$, the field is zero and the boundary condition is free.
The four vertices $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$ are distinct.

conclusion: $U_4 = -2Z^{-2}\sum_{\partial n_1 = A,\, \partial n_2 = \emptyset} w(n_1)w(n_2)\,\mathbf{1}[x_1,\dots,x_4 \text{ connected}] \le 0$ with $A = \{x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4\}$.

proofs.name: Switching and a count of pairings
proofs.slogan: Switch the sources in each product of two-point functions, then count how the four sources can be paired by clusters.
proofs.scope: The identity and the inequality for every finite graph with nonnegative couplings and four distinct vertices.

roles.why: Nonnegative couplings make all current weights nonnegative, so the final sum has a sign.
Distinct vertices make the symmetric difference of each pair of sources equal to all four points.

steps.slogan: Write every correlation as a ratio of sums over [random currents](c:random-current).
steps.detail: Expanding the Boltzmann factors gives $\mu[\sigma_B] = \sum_{\partial n = B} w(n)/Z$. A product of two [correlation functions](c:correlation-function) becomes a sum over pairs of currents with the two source sets.

steps.slogan: Move the second pair of sources to the first current with the switching lemma.
steps.detail: For each of the three pairings the switching lemma gives a sum over $\partial n_1 = A$, $\partial n_2 = \emptyset$ with the indicator that the second pair is connected in $n_1 + n_2$.

steps.slogan: Classify how the clusters of $n_1 + n_2$ split the four sources.
steps.detail: Each cluster holds an even number of sources by [parity](c:parity) of degrees. So either all four points are connected or the clusters pair them in one of three ways. The three indicators add up to $1 + 2\cdot\mathbf{1}[\text{all connected}]$.

steps.slogan: Subtract the three products from the four-point function and read off the sign.
steps.detail: The term $1$ reproduces $\mu[\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_3\sigma_4]$ and cancels it. What remains is $-2Z^{-2}$ times a sum of nonnegative weights over currents that connect all four points.

new_concepts.reminder: A random current is a random integer-valued function on edges whose odd-degree vertices form a prescribed source set.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ with coupling constants $\beta J_{xy}\ge0$, a current is a function $n:E\to\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, and its source set $\partial n$ is the set of vertices $x$ with $\sum_yn_{xy}$ odd. The weight of $n$ is $w(n)=\prod_{xy\in E}(\beta J_{xy})^{n_{xy}}/n_{xy}!$, and the random current with sources $A$ has law proportional to $w(n)\mathbf 1\{\partial n=A\}$. Expanding each factor $e^{\beta J_{xy}\sigma_x\sigma_y}$ in a power series gives $\langle\prod_{x\in A}\sigma_x\rangle=\sum_{\partial n=A}w(n)/\sum_{\partial n=\emptyset}w(n)$.

statement: For a ferromagnetic [Ising model](c:ising-model) in a nonnegative field $\mu$, every third [partial derivative](c:partial-derivative) of $\log Z_n$ with respect to the fields is $\le 0$. So each magnetization is a [concave function](c:concave-function) of the field along nonnegative directions.

hypotheses.text: The coupling matrix is symmetric with zero diagonal and $Q_{ij} \ge 0$, and $\beta > 0$.
The external field satisfies $\mu_i \ge 0$ for every site $i$.

conclusion: $\dfrac{\partial^3 \log Z_n}{\partial \mu_i\,\partial \mu_j\,\partial \mu_k} \le 0$ for all $i, j, k$.

proofs.name: Four replicas and a rotation
proofs.slogan: Write the third cumulant over four replicas, rotate the replica spins, and count parities site by site.
proofs.scope: All finite ferromagnetic Ising models with nonnegative field and all index triples.

roles.why: Nonnegative couplings make the rotated exponential a power series with nonnegative coefficients.
A nonnegative field enters only through the variable $a$ with a nonnegative coefficient, so the coefficients stay nonnegative.

steps.slogan: Write the third [cumulant](c:cumulant) as an expectation over four independent replicas.
steps.detail: With four independent copies, $u = E[(X^1_i - X^2_i)(X^1_j - X^3_j)(X^1_k - X^4_k)]$, which follows by expanding the eight products.

steps.slogan: Rotate the four replica spins at each site by an orthogonal Hadamard map.
steps.detail: The new variables $a, b, c, d$ keep the quadratic interaction diagonal, put the whole field on $a$, and turn the three differences into $c + d$, $b + d$ and $b + c$.

steps.slogan: Compute the sign of every one-site moment of the rotated variables.
steps.detail: A one-site moment is positive when all four exponents are even, equal to $-8$ when all four are odd, and zero when the [parity](c:parity) of the exponents is mixed.

steps.slogan: Expand the exponential as a [power series](c:power-series) with nonnegative coefficients.
steps.detail: The interaction adds even total degree in $b$, $c$ and $d$. Only the prefactor terms $c_id_jb_k$ and $d_ib_jc_k$ survive, and each forces an odd number of all-odd sites.

steps.slogan: An odd number of negative site factors makes every surviving term nonpositive.
steps.detail: Every monomial contributes a nonnegative coefficient times a product with an odd number of negative factors, so $Z_n^4 u \le 0$.

statement: For the nearest-neighbour [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with zero field, the [free energy](c:free-energy) per site is $\psi(\beta) = \log 2 + \frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{2\pi} \log\bigl[\cosh^2(2\beta) - \sinh(2\beta)(\cos\theta_1 + \cos\theta_2)\bigr]\,d\theta_1\,d\theta_2$.

hypotheses.text: The model is the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with unit nearest-neighbour coupling and zero field, on $n \times n$ [tori](c:torus).
The inverse temperature satisfies $\beta > 0$, so $x = \tanh\beta \in (0,1)$.

conclusion: $\psi(\beta) = \log 2 + \frac{1}{8\pi^2}\iint \log[\cosh^2(2\beta) - \sinh(2\beta)(\cos\theta_1 + \cos\theta_2)]\,d\theta_1 d\theta_2$.

proofs.name: High-temperature expansion and Kac–Ward determinants
proofs.slogan: Write the torus partition function through Kac–Ward determinants, factor them by Fourier modes, and take the limit of Riemann sums.
proofs.scope: The square lattice with unit couplings and zero field at every $\beta > 0$.

roles.why: Translation invariance of the square lattice on the torus lets Fourier modes factor the determinant.
Weights in $(0,1)$ make the Kac–Ward symbol positive away from one point of the torus.

steps.slogan: Expand the [partition function](c:partition-function) over even subgraphs with weight $\tanh\beta$.
steps.detail: The identity $e^{\beta\sigma\sigma'} = \cosh\beta\,(1 + \tanh\beta\,\sigma\sigma')$ gives $\psi = \log 2 + 2\log\cosh\beta + \log Z_x$.

steps.slogan: Compute the Kac–Ward [determinant](c:determinant) of the one-vertex torus.
steps.detail: The $4 \times 4$ determinant is $(1+x^2)^2 - x(1-x^2)(z + 1/z + w + 1/w)$, which is positive on the unit torus except possibly at $(1,1)$.

steps.slogan: Factor the determinant of the large torus over discrete [Fourier](c:fourier-coefficients) modes.
steps.detail: Lemma 4.1 of the source writes the determinant on $G_{nn}$ as a product of the symbol over $n$-th roots of $\pm1$, so its logarithm is a Riemann sum.

steps.slogan: Squeeze the squared partition function between three Kac–Ward determinants.
steps.detail: Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 of the source give $P^{-1,1} \le Z^2 \le \tfrac94\max(P^{-1,-1}, P^{-1,1}, P^{1,-1})$ on each torus.

steps.slogan: Pass from Riemann sums to the integral of the logarithm of the symbol.
steps.detail: Riemann sums converge, with bounded convergence at the critical weight, so $\log Z_x = \frac{1}{8\pi^2}\iint \log P\,d\theta\,d\varphi$.

steps.slogan: Rewrite the symbol in hyperbolic functions to reach Onsager's form of the [free energy](c:free-energy).
steps.detail: With $x = \tanh\beta$ the symbol is $[\cosh^2 2\beta - \sinh 2\beta(\cos\theta + \cos\varphi)]/\cosh^4\beta$, and the factor $\cosh^{-4}\beta$ cancels $2\log\cosh\beta$.

new_concepts.definition: For a lattice spin model with [partition function](c:partition-function) $Z_\Lambda(\beta)$ in a finite box $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the pressure is the [thermodynamic limit](c:thermodynamic-limit) $\psi(\beta)=\lim_{\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb Z^d}|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. statement: Below the [critical temperature](c:critical-temperature), the [spontaneous magnetization](c:spontaneous-magnetization) of the planar [Ising model](c:ising-model) with couplings $J_1, J_2$ is $m^*(\beta) = (1 - k^2)^{1/8}$ with $k = (\sinh 2\beta J_1 \sinh 2\beta J_2)^{-1}$. For equal couplings, $m^*(\beta) = (1 - \sinh(2\beta)^{-4})^{1/8}$.

proofs.name: Toeplitz determinant and the strong Szegő theorem
proofs.slogan: Write the row correlation as a Toeplitz determinant, then let Szegő's strong limit theorem compute its limit.
proofs.scope: Temperatures below the critical temperature. The cases $T \ge T_c$ are excluded.

roles.why: The free-fermion structure of the planar model gives the Toeplitz formula for row correlations.
Below the critical temperature the Onsager symbol has zero winding, so the strong Szegő theorem applies.

steps.slogan: Express the row correlation as a [Toeplitz determinant](c:toeplitz-determinant) of the Onsager symbol.
steps.detail: Montroll, Potts and Ward showed $\langle\sigma_{1,1}\sigma_{1,1+n}\rangle = D_n(\varphi_{ons})$, and the magnetization squared is the limit of this correlation.

steps.slogan: Compute the [Fourier coefficients](c:fourier-coefficients) of the logarithm of the symbol below $T_c$.
steps.detail: For $k < 1$ both $\gamma_1, \gamma_2$ lie in $(0,1)$, the symbol has zero [winding number](c:winding-number), and $(\log\varphi)_{\pm\ell} = \mp(\gamma_1^\ell - \gamma_2^\ell)/(2\ell)$.

steps.slogan: Apply the strong Szegő limit to the Toeplitz determinants of the symbol.
steps.detail: For a smooth symbol with zero winding and $(\log\varphi)_0 = 0$, the determinants tend to $\exp\sum_\ell \ell(\log\varphi)_\ell(\log\varphi)_{-\ell}$, which here equals $[(1-\gamma_1^2)(1-\gamma_2^2)/(1-\gamma_1\gamma_2)^2]^{1/4}$.

steps.slogan: Simplify the limit in terms of the couplings with hyperbolic identities.
steps.detail: Elementary algebra with $z_1 = \tanh\beta J_1$ and $z_2^* = e^{-2\beta J_2}$ turns the ratio into $1 - k^2$, so the row correlation tends to $(1-k^2)^{1/4}$.

steps.slogan: Identify the square root of the limit with the plus-state magnetization.
steps.detail: The source cites results that the physical magnetization equals this square root below $T_c$, and the physical magnetization is $\mu^+_\beta[\sigma_0]$.

new_concepts.name: critical temperature
new_concepts.reminder: The critical temperature $T_c=1/(k_B\beta_c)$ separates the disordered phase at high temperature from the ordered phase at low temperature.
new_concepts.definition: The critical temperature $T_c$ of a spin model is the temperature at which the model passes from a disordered phase, with a unique [Gibbs measure](c:gibbs-measure), to an ordered phase. For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) at $h=0$, the critical inverse temperature is $\beta_c=\inf\{\beta\ge0:m^*(\beta)>0\}$, where $m^*$ is the [spontaneous magnetization](c:spontaneous-magnetization), and $T_c=1/(k_B\beta_c)$.

new_concepts.name: Gibbs measure
new_concepts.reminder: A Gibbs measure is an infinite-volume law whose conditional law in each finite box is the finite Gibbs distribution.
new_concepts.definition: For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and a [boundary condition](c:boundary-condition) $\eta$, let $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ be the finite-volume [Gibbs distribution](c:gibbs-distribution) of an interaction in $\Lambda$, with the spins outside $\Lambda$ fixed to $\eta$. A [probability measure](c:probability-measure) $\mu$ on the configuration space $S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ is a Gibbs measure if, for every finite $\Lambda$, the [conditional distribution](c:conditional-distribution) of the spins in $\Lambda$ given the spins outside $\Lambda$ is $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ for $\mu$-almost every outside configuration $\eta$. These conditions are the DLR equations.

It is the parameter in the [Boltzmann distribution](c:boltzmann-distribution) $\mu_\beta(\sigma)=e^{-\beta H(\sigma)}/Z(\beta)$ of a [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian) $H$. Mathematical texts usually set $k_B=1$ and use $\beta\in[0,\infty)$ as the parameter.

new_concepts.name: phase transition
new_concepts.reminder: A phase transition is a parameter value where the infinite-volume free energy is not analytic or several Gibbs measures coexist.
new_concepts.definition: A phase transition of a lattice model is a value of its parameters, such as the inverse temperature $\beta$ and the field $h$, at which the infinite-volume [free energy](c:free-energy) is not real-analytic. It is first-order when a first derivative of the free energy is discontinuous there. In the [Ising model](c:ising-model) this happens at $h=0$ and $\beta>\beta_c$, where the derivative in $h$ jumps and several infinite-volume [Gibbs measures](c:gibbs-measure) coexist.

new_concepts.name: spontaneous magnetization
new_concepts.reminder: The spontaneous magnetization $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the magnetization that remains when the external field vanishes.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb Z^d$ at [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature) $\beta$, the spontaneous magnetization is $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$, where $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the infinite-volume state in the field $h>0$. It equals $\langle\sigma_0\rangle^+_\beta$, the [expected value](c:expected-value) of the spin at the origin under the plus Gibbs measure at $h=0$, and also the right derivative $\partial\psi/\partial h(\beta,0^+)$ of the pressure. For $d\ge2$, $m^*(\beta)=0$ for $\beta\le\beta_c$ and $m^*(\beta)>0$ for $\beta>\beta_c$.

statement: For the nearest-neighbour [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the [spontaneous magnetization](c:spontaneous-magnetization) is zero for $\beta < \beta_c$ and positive for $\beta > \beta_c$, with [critical temperature](c:critical-temperature) given by $\beta_c = \tfrac12\log(1+\sqrt2)$, that is $\sinh(2\beta_c) = 1$. For the [random-cluster model](c:random-cluster-model) with $q \ge 1$, $p_c(q) = \sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$.

hypotheses.text: The lattice is $\mathbb{Z}^2$, a [planar graph](c:planar-graph) isomorphic to its dual.
The coupling is ferromagnetic and equal to $1$ on nearest-neighbour edges, with plus [boundary condition](c:boundary-condition).

conclusion: $\beta_c = \tfrac12\log(1+\sqrt2)$, and more generally $p_c(q) = \sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$ for $q \ge 1$.

proofs.name: Self-duality plus sharpness
proofs.slogan: Self-duality gives crossing probabilities near one half at the self-dual point, and sharpness turns this into the critical point.
proofs.scope: The Ising model on the square lattice, and the random-cluster model on the square lattice with $q \ge 1$.

roles.why: Planarity and self-duality of the square lattice give the duality relation and the crossing identity.
A ferromagnetic coupling with plus boundary condition is what the coupling to the wired random-cluster model needs.

steps.slogan: Rewrite the magnetization as a connection probability in the [random-cluster model](c:random-cluster-model).
steps.detail: The Edwards–Sokal coupling with $p = 1 - e^{-2\beta}$ gives $m^*(\beta) = \phi^1_{p,2}[0 \leftrightarrow \infty]$, so it suffices to find $p_c(2)$.

steps.slogan: Show with Euler's formula that the dual configuration is again a random-cluster model.
steps.detail: The dual of $\phi^1_{p,q}$ is $\phi^0_{p^*,q}$ with $pp^*/((1-p)(1-p^*)) = q$, whose fixed point is $p_{sd} = \sqrt q/(1+\sqrt q)$.

steps.slogan: Compare crossing probabilities of a rectangle at the self-dual point.
steps.detail: A rectangle is crossed by the configuration or its rotated version is crossed by the dual, which gives $\phi^1_{p_{sd}}[H_n] \ge \tfrac12 \ge \phi^0_{p_{sd}}[H_n]$.

steps.slogan: Use sharpness of the [phase transition](c:phase-transition) to show $p_c \le p_{sd}$.
steps.detail: Below $p_c$ connection probabilities decay exponentially by the theorem of Duminil-Copin, Raoufi and Tassion, but at $p_{sd}$ they are at least of order $1/n$.

steps.slogan: Rule out an infinite free cluster at the self-dual point to show $p_{sd} \le p_c$.
steps.detail: An infinite cluster would make crossing probabilities tend to one, against the bound one half, and below $p_{sd}$ the wired measure is dominated by the free one.

steps.slogan: Translate the critical parameter back into the Ising [critical temperature](c:critical-temperature).
steps.detail: The critical parameter $p_c(2) = \sqrt2/(1+\sqrt2)$ gives $1 - p_c = 1/(1+\sqrt2)$, and the relation $\beta_c = -\tfrac12\log(1-p_c)$ from the coupling then gives $\beta_c = \tfrac12\log(1+\sqrt2)$.

new_concepts.reminder: Bernoulli percolation keeps each edge of a graph independently with probability $p$ and studies the connected clusters.

Its law is the [product measure](c:product-measure) $\mathbb P_p=\bigotimes_{e\in E}\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$ on $\{0,1\}^E$. new_concepts.name: Potts model
new_concepts.reminder: The Potts model gives each vertex one of $q$ states and rewards neighbors that are in the same state.
new_concepts.definition: The $q$-state Potts model on a finite [graph](c:graph) $G=(V,E)$ is the [Gibbs distribution](c:gibbs-distribution) on $\{1,\dots,q\}^V$ given by $\mu_\beta(\sigma)=Z^{-1}\exp(\beta\sum_{xy\in E}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_x=\sigma_y\})$. Its Hamiltonian is $H(\sigma)=-\sum_{xy\in E}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_x=\sigma_y\}$, and $\beta>0$ gives the ferromagnetic model. For $q=2$ it is the [Ising model](c:ising-model) at inverse temperature $\beta/2$.

new_concepts.name: random-cluster model
new_concepts.reminder: The random-cluster model weights an edge set $\omega$ by $p^{|\omega|}(1-p)^{|E\setminus\omega|}q^{k(\omega)}$, with $k(\omega)$ the number of clusters.
new_concepts.definition: The random-cluster model on a finite [graph](c:graph) $G=(V,E)$ with parameters $p\in[0,1]$ and $q>0$ is the probability measure on edge sets $\omega\subseteq E$ given by $\phi_{p,q}(\omega)=Z^{-1}p^{|\omega|}(1-p)^{|E\setminus\omega|}q^{k(\omega)}$. Here $k(\omega)$ is the number of [connected components](c:connected-component) of $(V,\omega)$, isolated vertices included. For $q=1$ it is [Bernoulli percolation](c:percolation), and for integer $q\ge2$ the Edwards–Sokal coupling links it to the [Potts model](c:potts-model) with $p=1-e^{-\beta}$.

new_concepts.reminder: The spontaneous magnetization $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the magnetization that remains when the external field vanishes.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb Z^d$ at [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature) $\beta$, the spontaneous magnetization is $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$, where $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the infinite-volume state in the field $h>0$. It equals $\langle\sigma_0\rangle^+_\beta$, the [expected value](c:expected-value) of the spin at the origin under the plus Gibbs measure at $h=0$, and also the right derivative $\partial\psi/\partial h(\beta,0^+)$ of the pressure. For $d\ge2$, $m^*(\beta)=0$ for $\beta\le\beta_c$ and $m^*(\beta)>0$ for $\beta>\beta_c$.

statement: The number of [domino tilings](c:domino-tiling) of a simply connected lattice region is $\sqrt{|\det K|}$, where $K$ is the [adjacency matrix](c:adjacency-matrix) of the dual graph with weight $1$ on horizontal and $i$ on vertical edges. For the $m \times n$ rectangle this gives $T(m,n) = \prod_{j=1}^{m}\prod_{k=1}^{n}\bigl(4\cos^2\tfrac{\pi j}{m+1} + 4\cos^2\tfrac{\pi k}{n+1}\bigr)^{1/4}$.

hypotheses.text: The region is a union of lattice squares bounded by a simple closed lattice polygon, a [Jordan curve](c:jordan-curve).
For the product formula, the region is the $m \times n$ rectangle.

conclusion: The number of tilings is $\sqrt{|\det K|}$, and for the rectangle it equals the product formula above.

proofs.name: Kasteleyn's sign argument and the eigenvalues of the grid
proofs.slogan: Show that every matching term of the determinant has the same phase, then diagonalize the rectangle matrix with sine waves.
proofs.scope: Simply connected lattice regions for the determinant formula, and rectangles for the product formula. Regions with holes and tori are excluded.

roles.why: Without holes, an alternating cycle encloses an even number of vertices, so all terms share one phase.
The rectangle is a product of two paths, so products of sine waves are eigenvectors.

steps.slogan: Turn domino tilings into [perfect matchings](c:perfect-matching) of a bipartite dual graph.
steps.detail: Each domino covers two neighbouring squares. With a chessboard colouring the dual graph is a [bipartite graph](c:bipartite-graph), so $K$ has the block form with a white-black block $A$ and $|\det K| = |\det A|^2$.

steps.slogan: Match the nonzero terms of the [determinant](c:determinant) with the tilings.
steps.detail: A term of $\det A$ is nonzero exactly when its permutation pairs neighbours, and each such term has modulus one because all weights are $1$ or $i$.

steps.slogan: Compare two matchings along one alternating cycle and show that their terms agree.
steps.detail: A cycle of length $2k$ gives the sign $(-1)^{k-1}$ from the permutation and $(-1)^{n+k+1}$ from the weights. The $n$ enclosed vertices are matched among themselves, so $n$ is even.

steps.slogan: Diagonalize the rectangle matrix with products of sine waves.
steps.detail: The functions $\sin\frac{\pi j x}{m+1}\sin\frac{\pi k y}{n+1}$ are an orthogonal basis of [eigenvectors](c:eigenvector) with [eigenvalues](c:eigenvalue) $2\cos\frac{\pi j}{m+1} + 2i\cos\frac{\pi k}{n+1}$.

steps.slogan: Take the modulus of the eigenvalue product and its square root.
steps.detail: Each eigenvalue has squared modulus $4\cos^2\frac{\pi j}{m+1} + 4\cos^2\frac{\pi k}{n+1}$, so the square root of $|\det K|$ is the product of their fourth roots.

concepts.c:domino-tiling: The formula counts domino tilings of a lattice region.
concepts.c:adjacency-matrix: The Kasteleyn matrix is a weighted adjacency matrix of the dual graph.
concepts.c:jordan-curve: A simple closed boundary makes every alternating cycle enclose an even number of vertices.
concepts.c:perfect-matching: Domino tilings are the perfect matchings of the dual graph.
concepts.c:bipartite-graph: The chessboard colouring makes the dual graph bipartite and the matrix block shaped.
concepts.c:determinant: The determinant expansion has one nonzero term for each tiling.
concepts.c:eigenvector: Products of sine waves are the eigenvectors of the rectangle matrix.
concepts.c:eigenvalue: The determinant of the rectangle matrix is the product of its eigenvalues.

source.ref: R. Kenyon, An introduction to the dimer model, arXiv:math/0310326, Theorem 1 (p. 1) with its proof and Lemma 1 (pp. 1-2), and Section 2.2 Rectangles (p. 3).
source.note: The steps follow Kenyon's proof of Kasteleyn's theorem and his eigenvalue computation for rectangles. The sign rule for one cycle is the source's Lemma 1.
